what: Sensitivity analysis for G1: each ported engine quirk was deliberately regressed in the Rust source, the wheel rebuilt, and scripts/rustport/reconcile_engine.py re-run. A quirk whose mutant still PASSES is a quirk the recorded corpora do not exercise -- '0 mismatches' says nothing about it, and only the 10^4-game lockstep fuzz (deferred to the Workflow) can cover it.

mutants.quirk: tied-feature scoring: every player tied for most meeples scores full points (vendored fix; upstream awarded nobody)
opposite_farmer_side TRT -> BRB (upstream typo was BRR, which made farm adjacency asymmetric)
mutants.golden_leg: FAIL (1 mismatch, at ply ~1611 of the leg)

mutants.quirk: meeple tuples in string_representation follow placed_meeples LIST INSERTION order, not a sort

remove_meeples_and_collect_points rebinds its `coordinate` local inside the 3x3 cloister scan, so each outer row re-derives its COLUMN range from the last tile seen (the outer ROW range is fixed from the original coordinate)
mutants.golden_leg: PASS (not discriminated by the 12 golden games)
mutants.all_corpora_leg: FAIL (86 mismatches; first at champ/28000000002 ply 29, kind string_representation)
mutants.note: This is the quirk most likely to be missed by a from-memory port, and the golden leg alone would have let it through. The 449-game champ corpus catches it.

mutants.quirk: RoadUtil.find_roads does NOT dedup -- Python `Road` has no __eq__/__hash__, so its set() keeps one entry per road-typed side, and a straight-road tile yields the same road twice
mutants.note: NOT a gate hole: the duplicate is provably a no-op. The first pass removes the road's meeples, so the second finds meeple_counts == 0, hits the `if sum(...) == 0: continue` guard, and scores nothing. The Rust port keeps the un-deduped form anyway (faithfulness over reasoning), but this is the one ported quirk with no empirical backing -- it rests on an argument, not a measurement.

conclusion: 4 of 5 quirks are empirically discriminated by the G1 corpora; the 5th is provably outcome-equivalent. The corpus is sensitive, so the 0-mismatch verdict is informative rather than vacuous.
